main_body: A well-like structure: a slate-blue roof canopy on two wooden posts, with a grey stone basin holding water below.
top_band: Column x=16: a thin cap at rows 1-2 (L=158/130) under the outline. Rows 3-14 are the roof's vertical tile stripes, drawn face-on. The basin has a light rim at row 30 and water at rows 31-34, but it is a small part.
evidence: The roof is the largest part. It is drawn as a flat front view of vertical tile strips with only a 1-2 row light cap at the top, so no top slope reads as a surface. There is no front-edge line or eave shadow, and the posts are flat vertical strips. The basin is a fair 3/4 piece (rim at row 30, water at rows 31-34, front rim at row 35, front face at rows 36-42). But the roof, a major part, is a front elevation, so the whole drawing fails.

style.evidence: The measured facts are far below both references: 9 colours per tile against 17 and 20, and 23 distinct colours against 40 and 38. All dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), against 1% and 33% in the references, so the outline is a near-black sticker line instead of a tinted material tone. The roof has about 5 lightness steps, but the posts and the basin front are mostly flat fills (the stone front is one L=104 run over 6 rows) with little grain. A careful artist would find it thinner than the references.
